godot imports custom attributes though the uv1-uv8 parameters.

The suggestion we tend to use is to half the precision etc.

> godot imports custom attributes though the uv1-uv8 parameters. Godot imports UV1-UV8, but UV1 and UV2 are read into `UV` and `UV2`, not into the CUSTOM shader built-ins. Here is how the glTF importer currently maps glTF attributes to Godot's shader built-ins: | Godot Shader Built-in | glTF Attribute(s) | Common Name | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `UV` | TEXCOORD_0 | UV1 | | `UV2` | TEXCOORD_1 | UV2 | | `CUSTOM0` | TEXCOORD_2, TEXCOORD_3 | UV3, UV4 | | `CUSTOM1` | TEXCOORD_4, TEXCOORD_5 | UV5, UV6 | | `CUSTOM2` | TEXCOORD_6, TEXCOORD_7 | UV7, UV8 | | **`CUSTOM3`** | **Not imported** | - | - |
After this PR: | Godot Shader Built-in | glTF Attribute(s) | Common Name | Alternative glTF Attribute | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `UV` | TEXCOORD_0 | UV1 | | | `UV2` | TEXCOORD_1 | UV2 | | | `CUSTOM0` | TEXCOORD_2, TEXCOORD_3 | UV3, UV4 | _CUSTOM0 | | `CUSTOM1` | TEXCOORD_4, TEXCOORD_5 | UV5, UV6 | _CUSTOM1 | | `CUSTOM2` | TEXCOORD_6, TEXCOORD_7 | UV7, UV8 | _CUSTOM2 | | **`CUSTOM3`** | **TEXCOORD_8, TEXCOORD_9** | **UV9, UV10** | **_CUSTOM3** | All the original attribute names are still supported, but simpler (single-attribute) alternatives are provided for the CUSTOM shader built-ins, and `CUSTOM3` is now supported.
> The suggestion we tend to use is to half the precision etc. Godot shaders already support `CUSTOM3`. There's no need to use mathematical tricks and overhead to pack multiple floats into one unless one needs even more custom values per vertex. A minor addition to the glTF importer gives access to `CUSTOM3`. I've already been using this code for several months, but wanted to make it available to the Godot community as there's no reason why `CUSTOM3` shouldn't be supported by the importer (other than Blender's 8 UV limitation when relying on "TEXTCOORD" attributes). This PR makes `CUSTOM3` available even in Blender exports via the "_CUSTOM3" attribute, nicely bypassing its limitation.
I'll ask around the asset pipeline team to get a second opinion.

Definitely in favor of expanding support to TEXCOORD_8+9 even if Blender does not support them.

I think adding support for `_CUSTOM0..3` seems reasonable, too.

Basically, I'd be open to supporting _CUSTOM0..3 by default, and then since it's not actually specified anywhere, we could theoretically add an API like in #97756 to allow mapping any custom attribute names (like _FOO and _BAR ) instead of _CUSTOM0..3.  Since `_CUSTOM0..3` can just be default behavior, it doesn't preclude adding more UV map functionality in the future.

Another piece of future work might be to allow these to be in any format supported by Godot CUSTOM mesh data: SCALAR, VEC2, VEC4, as well as possibly FLOAT, half or UINT8/SINT8 precision.

> Basically, I'd be open to supporting _CUSTOM0..3 by default, and then since it's not actually specified anywhere, we could theoretically add an API like in #97756 to allow mapping any custom attribute names (like _FOO and _BAR ) instead of _CUSTOM0..3. Since `_CUSTOM0..3` can just be default behavior, it doesn't preclude adding more UV map functionality in the future. Name mapping can also be done in the 3D content creation software. I currently use Geometry Nodes in Blender to map other vertex attributes and object data to _CUSTOM0..3. Considering data will be coming in from many different domains, it would be rarely practical to enter values manually, so some mapping in the 3D content creation software is generally desirable anyway. For example, in my case, I have moving machine parts, each with its own animation parameters (e.g. pistons moving up and down here and a fan spinning there), all combined into a single mesh automatically using Geometry Nodes before exporting to Godot. This setup in Blender allows me to specify the pivot point and orientation of each machine part using the **object transform**, animation properties such as frequency and phase using **named attributes** ("TranslatioFreq", "RotationFreq", "SecondaryPhase", and so on), and the UV coordinates for a 3rd UV set I use for some animated trim sheet using the **UV editor**. All of this data, which comes from different parts of Blender, is then packed into _CUSTOM0..3 vertex attributes in one cohesive mesh that a Godot shader then animates efficiently on the GPU. (As a side note, I also unpack all of this in Blender and pass it to a Shader Node setup, so I can see all the parts animated in Blender as I edit them, and see exactly the same result I get in Godot before I even export). I'm not against the idea of #97756 for simpler setups though; it can be beneficial for people who don't want to use Geometry Nodes in Blender, especially if all of their data is already specified in the Vertex or Face Corner domain. The point I'm making is that the existing workflow is already more powerful and capable (with or without "_CUSTOM0...3", as the use of "TEXCOORD..." is almost as powerful, except for the `CUSTOM3` limitation).
> Another piece of future work might be to allow these to be in any format supported by Godot CUSTOM mesh data: SCALAR, VEC2, VEC4, as well as possibly FLOAT, half or UINT8/SINT8 precision. This would be interesting (and useful) if additional shader built-ins will be provided for custom data of different data types. If Godot will simply convert these different data types into the floats of `CUSTOM0..3`, then I think this too should be done in the 3D content creation software.
If necessary, we can also define a "_CUSTOM* custom gltf extension schema under the Godot Engine namespace.

In case it helps, here's a diff that shows what has been removed as well.

Most of the removals are related to replacing `resize` with `resize_initialized` in existing code. Additionally, I moved the `if (num_channels == 4)` statement to the `if (num_channels == 2 || num_channels == 4)` block since it relies on the vector resize operation there. The original code in that section was a recipe for future coding mistakes. The code (in that section) still has the same behavior, but is now much cleaner and simpler.
